content: Adding a 7th DOF (external linear rail) to a 6-DOF arm makes the system kinematically redundant: infinite joint solutions exist for a given TCP pose because the extra DOF must be resolved by a chosen strategy, not solved uniquely. Standard resolution strategies: (1) fix/parameterize the rail position via a heuristic (e.g. center the 6-DOF arm's reachable envelope around the target, or minimize rail travel from previous position), (2) Jacobian-based methods (damped least squares / pseudoinverse, null-space projection) for velocity-level redundancy resolution, (3) task augmentation adding a secondary objective (e.g. maximize manipulability, minimize joint travel). For an interview-scope project, a simple deterministic heuristic (e.g. solve rail position first via projecting target X onto rail range, then solve remaining 6-DOF IK) is far cheaper than a full Jacobian redundancy resolver and avoids underspecifying the problem.
